title: Investigation of anti-asthmatic constituents and mechanisms of Cimicifugae Rhizoma based on LC-MS analysis, network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Yin, Yi-Ming; Ji, Wen-Xuan; Yin, Jia; Li, Xin-Yu; Sheng, Tian-Yuan; Wei, Yi; Xu, Zhen-Peng; Shen, Tao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究升麻抗哮喘成分与机制，基于LC-MS、网络药理学和实验验证，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cimicifugae Rhizoma was used for the treatment of asthma in traditional Chinese medicine. The triterpenoid partition of Cimicifugae Rhizoma, named as 'Ximingting', is commercially used for perimenopausal syndrome. However, the anti-asthma constituents and mechanism of Cimicifugae Rhizoma, as well as the therapeutic effect of 'Ximingting' on asthma remain unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to illustrate anti-asthma constituents of Cimicifugae Rhizoma and 'Ximingting', and explore the underlying molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The ethyl acetate fraction of Cimicifugae Rhizoma extract (EAEC) was prepared accroding to the manufacturing process of 'Ximingting'. The chemical composition of EAEC were analyzed by UPLC-MS/MS. An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma mouse model was used for evaluating the bioassay in vivo. Network pharmacology was adopted for predicting anti-asthmatic targets/pathways, validated by molecular docking, ELISA, Western blot, qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and flow cytometry. RESULTS: Fifty-eight constituents (mainly triterpenoids) were identified in EAEC. EAEC significantly attenuated OVA-induced airway inflammatory infiltration, reduced inflammatory cytokines, and restored Th1/Th2 balance in mice. Network pharmacology indicated that anti-asthmatic effect of EAEC was related to inflammation, oxidative stress, and T-cell differentiation. Further experiments demonstrated that EAEC activated Keap1-Nrf2 signaling to enhance antioxidant capacity, and inhibited STAT6 phosphorylation and GATA3 expression, thereby blocking CD4(+) T cell differentiation into Th2 cells. CONCLUSION: Triterpenoids in Cimicifugae Rhizoma exert anti-asthmatic effects by activating Keap1-Nrf2 pathway against oxidative stress and regulating STAT6/GATA3 pathway to balance immunity. These findings reveal the anti-asthmatic mechanism of Cimicifugae Rhizoma and suggest the potential of 'Ximingting' for further anti-asthmatic investigation.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：升麻（Cimicifugae Rhizoma）在传统中医中用于治疗哮喘。升麻的三萜类组分，名为“希明婷”，在商业上用于围绝经期综合征。然而，升麻的抗哮喘成分及其机制，以及“希明婷”对哮喘的治疗效果仍不清楚。研究目的：本研究旨在阐明升麻和“希明婷”的抗哮喘成分，并探讨其潜在的分子机制。材料与方法：根据“希明婷”的制备工艺制备了升麻提取物的乙酸乙酯部位（EAEC）。通过UPLC-MS/MS分析了EAEC的化学成分。采用卵清蛋白（OVA）诱导的哮喘小鼠模型评估体内生物活性。通过网络药理学预测抗哮喘靶点/通路，并通过分子对接、ELISA、Western blot、qRT-PCR、免疫荧光和流式细胞术进行验证。结果：在EAEC中鉴定出58种成分（主要为三萜类化合物）。EAEC显著减轻了OVA诱导的气道炎症浸润，降低了炎症细胞因子，并恢复了小鼠的Th1/Th2平衡。网络药理学表明，EAEC的抗哮喘作用与炎症、氧化应激和T细胞分化相关。进一步实验证明，EAEC激活了Keap1-Nrf2信号以增强抗氧化能力，并抑制了STAT6磷酸化和GATA3表达，从而阻断CD4(+) T细胞向Th2细胞分化。结论：升麻中的三萜类化合物通过激活Keap1-Nrf2通路对抗氧化应激，并调节STAT6/GATA3通路以平衡免疫，从而发挥抗哮喘作用。这些发现揭示了升麻的抗哮喘机制，并提示“希明婷”在进一步抗哮喘研究中的潜力。
